method_note: YouTube figures were read on 2026-10-14 from public, logged-out YouTube pages (channel /videos tabs, search results, and watch pages) with hl=en&gl=US. Each video's exact view count and publish date come from the watch page's ytInitialData. Where only a rounded figure and relative age were visible, as on a channel grid or search listing, that is noted. Window is measured from 2026-10-14: last_7_days, last_30_days, last_90_days, last_12_months, older_than_12_months. View counts are point-in-time snapshots and keep changing.

cross_cutting.claim: Share of U.S. adults who say they ever use YouTube, by age
cross_cutting.value: Ages 50-64: 85%. Ages 65+: 64%. All adults: 84%. Ages 18-29: 95%. Ages 30-49: 92%. Survey of 5,022 U.S. adults fielded Feb 5 - Jun 18, 2025.
cross_cutting.source_title: Pew Research Center - Social Media and News / Social Media Fact Sheet

cross_cutting.claim: Facebook use among older U.S. adults, for comparison with YouTube
cross_cutting.value: Ages 50-64: 74%. Ages 65+: 57%. Same Pew 2025 survey, so YouTube reach is higher than Facebook in both older age groups.
cross_cutting.source_title: Pew Research Center - Social Media Fact Sheet

cross_cutting.claim: Growth in YouTube viewing on TV sets by older adults (Nielsen, U.S.)
cross_cutting.value: February 2025 YouTube viewing on TV compared with February 2023: adults 65+ up 96% ('nearly doubled'), adults 50-64 up 62%, total up 53%. Share of YouTube's TV audience in Feb 2025: 50-64 = 20.4%, 65+ = 15.4%. YouTube had 11.6% of total U.S. TV viewing that month.
cross_cutting.source_title: Nielsen - YouTube Achieves Best Monthly Performance to Date and Pulls Ahead in Nielsen's February Media Distributor Gauge

cross_cutting.claim: Latest YouTube share of total U.S. TV viewing (Nielsen Media Distributor Gauge)
cross_cutting.value: July 2026: YouTube reached a record 14.2% of TV viewing. This counts TV-set viewing only, not mobile or desktop. Nielsen notes upcoming methodology changes that may make later months not directly comparable.
cross_cutting.source_title: Nielsen - TV Usage Kicks Usual Summer Slowdown, Fueled by World Cup and Streaming in Nielsen's July Gauge Reports

cross_cutting.claim: TV is the primary device for YouTube viewing in the U.S.
cross_cutting.value: "TV is now the primary device for YouTube viewing in the U.S." (by watch time). Viewers watch "on average, over 1B hours of YouTube content on TVs daily". Footnoted as of December 2024.
cross_cutting.source_title: YouTube Official Blog - From the YouTube CEO: Our big bets for 2025 (Neal Mohan)

cross_cutting.claim: Creator share of watch-page ad revenue
cross_cutting.value: YouTube pays partners 55% of net revenues from ads displayed or streamed on their public videos on the Watch Page.
cross_cutting.source_title: YouTube Help - YouTube partner earnings overview

cross_cutting.claim: Monetization policy on mass-produced and templated content, which affects faceless or AI-assisted documentary channels
cross_cutting.value: On July 15, 2025 YouTube renamed 'repetitious content' to 'inauthentic content' (content that is 'repetitive or mass-produced'). Examples of content that cannot be monetized include 'Image slideshows, templated storylines, or scrolling text with minimal or no narrative, commentary, or educational value' and 'AI-generated content made with generic or unoriginal templates'. Reused content is allowed only if 'viewers can tell that there's a meaningful difference'.
cross_cutting.source_title: YouTube Help - YouTube channel monetization policies

cross_cutting.claim: Older viewers' preference for long-form content
cross_cutting.value: unknown. I found no Pew, Nielsen, or YouTube primary source that directly measures long-form preference by age. The best available proxy is above: older adults' YouTube viewing is growing fastest on TV screens (Nielsen Feb 2025).

rpm_evidence.label: RPM vs CPM definition
rpm_evidence.value_or_text: RPM: 'Revenue Per Mille (RPM) is a metric that represents how much money you've earned per 1,000 video views'. It is total revenue after YouTube's revenue share. CPM: 'Cost per 1,000 impressions (CPM) is a metric that represents how much advertisers are spending to show ads on YouTube'.

rpm_evidence.label: Creator revenue share on watch-page ads
rpm_evidence.value_or_text: YouTube pays partners 55% of net revenues from ads displayed or streamed on their public videos on the Watch Page.

rpm_evidence.label: Flippa listing 12813083: faceless history/mansions documentary channel
rpm_evidence.category: creator-reported (single channel, seller claim on a marketplace listing, not independently audited)
rpm_evidence.value_or_text: The seller claims RPM exceeding $20. U.S. accounts for 77.2% of views. 83% of the audience is 45+ and 41.7% is 65+. Most viewing is on TV devices. The channel started in August 2025. Headline and description figures conflict (views 12M vs 9M; revenue $256K vs $180,049.90; subscribers 98,123 vs 81.2K). The listing shows a 'Verified Listing' badge but also states financials are seller-provided.

rpm_evidence.label: Flippa listing 12979853: history/cultural-education channel
rpm_evidence.category: creator-reported (single channel, seller claim on a marketplace listing, not independently audited)
rpm_evidence.value_or_text: Claims a $13 average RPM, about 84K subscribers, and $33,677 gross revenue in the past year. 64% of the audience is in the U.S. Topic is African history / cultural education.

rpm_evidence.label: LearningRevolution YouTube earnings calculator
rpm_evidence.category: industry estimate (LearningRevolution.net; methodology not disclosed beyond 'creator income reports, YouTube Studio benchmark data, and advertising industry research')
rpm_evidence.value_or_text: History & Documentary: $4-$6 RPM (average $5) for a Tier 1 audience. $1-$2.50 for South/Southeast Asian audiences.

rpm_evidence.label: FlowShorts history niche page
rpm_evidence.category: industry estimate (FlowShorts; no methodology or source cited)

limitations: Do not average the RPM figures above into a niche RPM. They mix official definitions, unaudited seller claims from two single channels, and blog estimates with undisclosed methods.
Subscriber and view counts are YouTube's public rounded displays (channel grids, search listings) or exact watch-page counts captured on 2026-10-14. They change continuously.

Public YouTube pages do not show competitor audience age, geography, or RPM. No claim is made about the age profile of any listed channel's audience. The only age and geography data is the seller-reported Flippa listing.
Google Trends could not be read (HTTP 429 via fetch), so no search-trend data is included.

YouTube search results are personalized and region-dependent even when logged out. Queries used hl=en&gl=US. The 'this year' and all-time view-sorted searches are samples, not a complete census of each pillar.

WebFetch could not read YouTube pages because they are rendered by JavaScript. Data came from the in-app browser (early channels) and from server-rendered ytInitialData in public, logged-out page HTML (no API, no login).
The 'low-view saturation' observations (pillars 2, 4, 6, 11, 12) are qualitative and come from small samples of search results.
Exact data for ColdFusion's Enron video (e5qC1YGRMKI) could not be retrieved. Its listing figures are reported as displayed.
The Nielsen older-viewer growth figures (Feb 2025 vs Feb 2023) measure YouTube viewing on TV sets only, not total YouTube usage.
I did not find a primary source (Pew, Nielsen, Think with Google) that directly measures long-form preference among viewers 50+.
